newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine Finance Ministry on time with T-bill payments.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine Finance Ministry on time with T-bill payments.

text.p: Ukraine's Finance Ministry paid 83 million hryvnias ($47 million) in Treasury bill payments on time and was taking measures to preclude further delays, a top government official said on Thursday.
"We wouldn't want to lose buyers, and we are working within the ministry to ensure delays never happen again," Finance Minister Valentyn Koronevsky told reporters.
The ministry was up to a day late making interest and principal payments once in August and twice in September and officials made no comment on the delays at the time.

Koronevsky said the delays occurred because the ministry was directed to send large payments to regions of Ukraine where wages have gone unpaid for months. The total wage backlog stands at the equivalent of $1.7 billion.
Deputy Prime Minister Viktor Pynzenyk apologised last week for the delays and promised they would not be repeated.
The central bank plans to raise 150 trillion karbovanets this year in T-bill sales to go towards covering the projected 467 trillion karbovanets budget deficit.

Ukraine took the karbovanets out of circulation on September 16, when the hryvnia became the country's sole currency. The hryvnia, worth 100,000 karbovanets, has been unchanged at 1.76 to the dollar on the Ukraine Interbank Currency Exchange since being introduced in early September. --Natalya Zinets, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
